newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African links vital for region - trade minister.
newsitem.headline: South African links vital for region - trade minister.

text.p: South Africa's drive to improve trade and investment links with Zimbabwe and Zambia was vital to future regional stability, Trade and Industry Minister Alec Erwin said on Tuesday.
"The reason why we have moved to rapidly try and establish better links on an investment and trade basis with Zimbabwe and Zambia is not just to be nice guys," he told a media briefing.
"It fundamentally affects future stability of the area."
He said the rapid increase in South Africa's trade surplus with Zimbabwe could not be accounted for by the Zimbabwean growth rate, even though it was quite healthy.
"It is not possible for the Zimbabwean growth rate to bring about the shift of 70 to 80 percent," he said.
What was probably happening was that South African exporters were taking trade away from Zimbabwe's other trading partners, possibly in the European Union.
This was why South Africa had upgraded its bilateral agreement with Zimbabwe and South African Customs Union (SACU) members were negotiating assistance for Zambia.
The agreement with Zambia would be structurally more complex than the one with Zimbabwe.

Erwin said he did not want to open up a whole lot of bilateral trade agreements -- but Zambia stood out like a sore thumb in the region because it had no preferential access to the South African market.
The negotiations would be a precursor to the proposed Southern African Development Community (SADC) free trade agreement.
"We have agreed...that we are prepared to make a special dispensation for Zambia and get it in line with the other major trading partners," he said.
Attention would also have to be paid to providing some assistance to Maritius, which also did not have preferential access.
Erwin said he expected the details of the SADC free trade agreement, including controversial rules of origin specifics, to be finalised in six months' time.
